definition: Generating N candidate responses and keeping the best according to a reward model or verifier, either for serving (better answers at N-times cost) or for creating high-quality SFT data from the model's own best outputs.
details: Generating N candidate responses and keeping the best according to a reward model or verifier, either for serving (better answers at N-times cost) or for creating high-quality SFT data from the model's own best outputs.

explainer.lead: Rejection sampling here means generating N candidate responses and keeping the best one according to a reward model or verifier. It matters because it raises answer quality at N-times the cost, or produces high-quality supervised fine-tuning data from the model's own best outputs.

tiers.eli5: Ask the model for several answers, then have a judge pick the best one—either to show the user or to use as a training example.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers sample N outputs and score them with a verifier, selecting the top one for serving or for building SFT data. The pitfall is cost scaling linearly with N while gains diminish, and a weak verifier can pick confidently wrong answers.
tiers.paperLevel: Given N samples from the model and a scoring function, the method returns the sample with the highest score. Quality is bounded by the verifier's accuracy and by N; cost grows with N.

explainer.example: A system samples 16 responses to a question, scores each with a reward model, and returns the highest-scoring one.
